## By The Numbers: A Dominant Saturday

Let me walk you through the data from September 27th – and these numbers speak for themselves. We went 12-2 across 14 games for an 85.7% hit rate. That's not just good, that's statistically elite when you consider the baseline 50% probability in any given matchup.

## Confidence Level Analysis

Here's where it gets interesting. Our picks ranged from 50% confidence (Nationals) to 61% confidence (Cubs, Guardians, Mariners). The 61% confidence picks went 2-1, while our medium-confidence plays in the 54-60% range converted at an impressive 9-1 clip.

## The Misses: What The Data Showed

Two losses on the day – let's examine them. The Rays at 54% confidence failed to deliver against the Phillies, and our 61% confidence pick on the Guardians didn't hit against the Royals. Statistically, at 61% confidence, you expect to lose roughly 4 out of 10. These losses fall within expected variance.

## Performance Breakdown By Confidence Tier

When I segment the data by confidence levels, here's what emerges:

**High Confidence (60%+):** 2-1 record (66.7% hit rate)

**Medium Confidence (54-59%):** 7-1 record (87.5% hit rate)

**Lower Confidence (50-53%):** 3-0 record (100% hit rate)

Interestingly, our medium-confidence tier outperformed across the board today. This suggests our model's sweet spot is identifying value in the 54-59% probability range.

## What This Means Going Forward

An 85.7% daily accuracy rate is significant – approximately 2.45 standard deviations above the 50% baseline expectation. However, one day is just one data point. The key metric I'm tracking is consistency across sample size. Over larger samples (30+ days), we're looking for sustained accuracy in the 58-62% range to demonstrate true edge.

No games scheduled for tomorrow, which gives us time to analyze today's results and refine our models before the next slate.
